user_question: Create a choropleth map of hospital counts across Centre County.

outputs.summary: Workflow completed with accepted terminal artifacts. Active commitments: analytical_spatial_unit=Centre County census tracts

workflow_plan.goal: Create a choropleth map of hospital counts across Centre County.

workflow_steps.title: Count hospitals by census tract
workflow_steps.purpose: Spatially aggregate the hospital point features into the Centre County census tract polygons.
workflow_steps.instructions: Count point features from input_1 within the polygons in input_2. Produce a GeoPackage polygon layer containing the tract features and the derived hospital-count attribute. Do not assume or rename source fields; runtime QC should verify the resulting count field.

workflow_steps.title: Map hospital counts by tract
workflow_steps.purpose: Generate the final choropleth map from the tract polygons enriched with hospital counts.
workflow_steps.instructions: Create an HTML choropleth map from counted_tracts. Visualize the runtime-grounded hospital-count attribute; leave the field parameter unset until schema QC identifies the derived count field.

requirements.scope: Hospital point and census tract polygon inputs must be supported GeoPackage vector datasets for point_count_by_polygon.
Hospital points and census tract polygons must use compatible CRSs for spatial counting.
Hospital points and census tract polygons must have valid, non-empty geometries for spatial counting.
The polygon aggregation must cover Centre County at the selected census-tract analytical unit.
The thematic mapping input must be a supported vector GeoPackage and the terminal output must be HTML.
The counted tract layer must contain a runtime-grounded field representing the number of hospitals for thematic mapping.

commitments.rationale: The goal requests counts across Centre County without specifying an analytical unit, and the supplied inputs provide both census tracts and county subdivisions. Census tracts are selected as the explicit choropleth unit.
